title: Define agent role prompts + chain-of-command routing rules
description:
Define system prompt templates that match the operating hierarchy and routing policy:

Hierarchy:
- CEO (human) → main (root agent) → pdpm (manager) → dev/qa (workers)

Routing guardrail (must be encoded in prompts):
- main must not directly dispatch/instruct dev/qa; must route via pdpm.
- CEO override is allowed (explicitly documented).

Deliverables are docs (no code): role prompt templates + escalation rules + bd workflow conventions.

## ✅ PASS — mc-b1j.10: Signed Session Tokens

**PR:** https://github.com/2lab-ai/ocmc/pull/2
**Branch:** feat/signed-session-tokens
**Commit:** d581977

### Implementation Summary
Replaced plaintext mc_session=<username> cookie with HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens.

Token format: base64url(JSON{u, iat, exp}).hex(HMAC-SHA256)

### Acceptance Criteria Evidence

| Criteria | Status |
|----------|--------|
| Login sets signed token cookie | PASS |
| Unauthorized API calls return 401 | PASS |
| Logout clears cookie | PASS |
| HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax | PASS |
| Token expiry (24h default) | PASS |
| Config via env var (MC_SESSION_SECRET) | PASS |
| Constant-time comparison | PASS |
| Unit tests (8 passing) | PASS |
| Meaningful commit | PASS |
| Push/PR | PASS (PR #2) |

### Test Results
running 8 tests - all ok
test_create_and_verify_token, test_wrong_secret_rejected,
test_tampered_payload_rejected, test_expired_token_rejected,
test_malformed_token_rejected, test_empty_username_rejected,
test_cookie_format, test_clear_cookie

Design: Chose HMAC-signed stateless tokens over DB-backed sessions. No DB round-trip per request, same security for cookie-forgery prevention.

title: Policy guardrails + CEO override (routing enforcement)
description:
Implements PRD v2.1 governance: chain-of-command routing rules + default root-only direct control + CEO break-glass override.

Scope:
- Central policy engine that authorizes/denies every mutating endpoint (task move/assign, agent changes, cron, project intake)
- Enforce: main cannot directly control/dispatch to dev*/qa* without CEO override context
- Enforce: pdpm can control its own child workers
- Root-only direct control for CEO/user by default (root=main)
- CEO Override session: time-bounded, requires reason, visibly represented, and audit-logged
- Audit must capture BOTH allowed and denied attempts with override metadata

This task should produce an explicit authorization matrix and unit tests for it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Policy engine exists as a single module/function used by all mutating handlers
- [ ] Without override: user direct-control is limited to root surface (root=main)
- [ ] Without override: main → dev*/qa* direct control/dispatch attempts are denied
- [ ] With override: CEO/user can control any agent/task; override requires reason + TTL
- [ ] Denied actions return 403 and are audit-logged with actor+target+deny_reason
- [ ] Allowed actions are audit-logged; override metadata captured when used
- [ ] Unit tests cover the policy matrix (happy paths + denies)
- [ ] Meaningful commit referencing this issue id
- [ ] git push to master

title: Policy engine + routing guardrails (deny + audit + override)
description:
Implement PRD v2 routing guardrails in backend.

Core requirement:
- Default hierarchy: CEO(user) → main(root agent) → pdpm → dev
- main must NOT be able to directly control/dispatch to dev targets.
- CEO can override (explicit + reason + time-bounded) and every override must be audit-logged.

Deliverables:
1) Central policy engine (e.g., mc/policy.rs) with an authorization matrix that uses agents.role + parent_id.
2) Apply guardrails to all mutating endpoints (at minimum: task.assign, task.move, agent mutations; plus cron if present).
3) API contract for override: payload fields {override: bool, override_reason: string} (or header) and TTL semantics.
4) Audit logging:
   - on deny: action=policy.deny with attempted action + target
   - on allow with override: action=<action> with override=true + reason

Note: This task is backend enforcement; UI work is tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Policy engine implements allow/deny for (actor_kind=user|agent) × (actor_id) × (action) × (target_agent)
- [ ] main→dev direct control attempts are denied (HTTP 403) and logged as policy.deny
- [ ] pdpm→dev (its child) is allowed
- [ ] CEO override path exists (explicit flag + reason) and is audit-logged
- [ ] Guardrails wired into: POST /api/task/:id/assign, POST /api/task/:id/move, agent hierarchy mutations
- [ ] Unit tests cover policy matrix (at least 10 cases)
- [ ] Meaningful commit(s) referencing this issue id
- [ ] git push + PR

title: Agent hierarchy API (CRUD + role/parent/reparent)
description:

- evaluate routing policy in mc-b1j.22

Required fields:
- role (root|pdpm|dev|qa|observer)
- parent_id (tree edge; main → pdpm* → dev*/qa*)

Suggested endpoints:
- GET /api/agents → list agents with role + parent_id
- POST /api/agents → create agent {id, display_name, role, parent_id}
- DELETE /api/agents/:id → delete agent (must forbid deleting root)
- POST /api/agents/:id/reparent {parent_id} → change parent (cycle check)

All hierarchy mutations must be policy-guarded + audit-logged.

- [ ] All endpoints require auth
